# Sandbox Configuration Model

Proposed standard for how `openshell-sandbox` decides what a sandbox gets:
which Claude account, which credentials, which network policy, and where
telemetry goes. **Draft for review.** The axes, segments, and selection UI
are unimplemented. The parts that shipped ahead of them, because home needed
them: `config/site.env` (§6.2), policy templating and the rendered
`openshell-policy.yaml` artifact (§5), and its upload into the sandbox.

Written because adding a "home" environment exposed that `--policy` and
`--profile` are two names for overlapping concerns.

**§1 is out of date and kept as written.** Since it was recorded: `code.yaml`
is `work.yaml`, `home` is a real profile (personal plus Prometheus and Loki
reads), `--profile` is required on `--create`/`--recreate` and on every
`scode`, there is no `DEFAULT_PROFILE`, and `policy_for_profile()` is gone —
profile name and policy filename are one word. Every file:line below predates
that. The proposal itself (§2 onward) is unchanged and still unimplemented.

## 1. Current state

### 1.1 What exists

| Concept | Where | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` | `scripts/sandbox.sh:161` | *(unset)* or `personal` |
| `--policy` | `scripts/sandbox.sh:160` | `code`, `research`, `personal`, `local`, or a path |
| profile → policy template | `policy_for_profile()`, called at `sandbox.sh:1144` | `personal` → `personal.yaml`, else `code.yaml` |
| site config | `config/site.env`, loaded at `sandbox.sh:19` | `OTEL_HOST`, `OTEL_PORT`, `PROMETHEUS_URL`, `LOKI_URL` — all required, no defaults |
| effective policy | `~/sandboxes/<name>/openshell-policy.yaml`, written by `render_policy()` | template with `site.env` substituted; uploaded, never downloaded |
| telemetry env | `/sandbox/.env`, written from `site.env` | `bin/claude.env` no longer sets endpoint or protocol |

`--profile` is stored in `manifest.json` and re-read on `--refresh`.

The site axis (§2.1) exists in a narrow form already: `config/site.env` is
gitignored, has no defaults, and `sandbox.sh` refuses to run without it. What
does not exist is `--site` as a named value — the file describes one machine
and is never selected between.

### 1.2 What is conflated

`personal` is a statement about **which Claude account** ("subscription, not
Vertex"), but it currently also decides:

- which policy template is chosen (`sandbox.sh:1144`)
- whether gcloud and gws credentials upload (`sandbox.sh:624`, `:1288`)
- whether Jira env vars are written (`sandbox.sh:1177`)
- whether Vertex/Google/Jira keys are stripped from `settings.json`
  (`sandbox.sh:560`)
- whether the Jira section is stripped from the sandbox system prompt
  (`sandbox.sh:695`)
- whether pulling a private repo prompts for confirmation
  (`sandbox.sh:340`, `:1029`, `scripts/lib.sh:238`)
- which OTEL resource attribute tags a session (`sandbox.sh:1231-1232`)
- what `bin/validate-profile.sh` expects to be reachable (`:110` onward)

Every one of those is a literal `== "personal"` or `!= "personal"` test, in
three files (`sandbox.sh`, `scode`, `bin/validate-profile.sh`) plus
`scripts/generate-pr-context.sh`.

### 1.3 Telemetry destination is no longer one of them

It used to be. `policies/personal.yaml` hardcoded `172.30.0.10:4318`, the
local collector on the work machine, so a personal sandbox at home pointed at
an address that does not exist there. Same account, different destination —
it varies with *where the host is*, not *which account signs in*, which is
the observation the `site` axis is built on.

That one is fixed ahead of the rest of this model, because home needed it:
the policy carries `${OTEL_HOST}`/`${OTEL_PORT}`, `render_policy()`
substitutes them from `config/site.env`, and `sandbox.sh` writes the matching
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` into `/sandbox/.env`. Verified working over
Tailscale (§7).

The other eight bullets above are untouched. `--profile personal` still
decides all of them.

### 1.4 Policy file duplication is already drifting

`code.yaml`, `personal.yaml`, and `research.yaml` carry byte-identical
`filesystem_policy`, `landlock`, and `process` blocks (25 lines each). The
package-registry blocks are near-identical — except `research.yaml` has no
`npm` and no `debian` entries, while the other two do. Nothing marks that as
deliberate. Three files, one already out of step.

## 2. Axes

### 2.1 `site` — where the host machine sits

Determines everything that is a **local address**: telemetry endpoints,
cluster services, LAN and tailnet reachability.

| Site | Telemetry |
|---|---|
| `work` | local collector containers (`172.30.0.10:4318` from a sandbox) |
| `home` | k3s cluster over Tailscale |

**Not "hardware".** The axis is the host's network position, not the
physical box. A second home machine is still `site: home`; naming it
hardware invites per-machine config files that all say the same thing.

Site is a static property of the machine, so it is **configured once, not
chosen per sandbox** (§6.1).

### 2.2 `access` — which Claude account

| Access | Auth | Credentials it requires |
|---|---|---|
| `vertex` | Vertex AI | gcloud ADC |
| `subscription` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or OAuth `.credentials.json` | none |

`access` means exactly one thing: how Claude authenticates, plus the
credentials that authentication itself needs. Jira, gws, and observability
access are **not** consequences of it — they are segments (§2.3).

### 2.3 `segments` — what the sandbox may reach

Everything else is a named policy segment, selected by slug. There is no
grouping layer, no implied set, and no mapping from an axis to a bundle of
segments. Each slug carries its own description and is picked directly.

Site and access do not *select* segments — they **filter** which slugs are
offered, and set which are pre-checked. §4 defines the mechanism.

### 2.4 The matrix

|  | `vertex` | `subscription` |
|---|---|---|
| `work` | supported (today: `code.yaml`) | supported (today: `personal.yaml`) |
| `home` | **not supported** | supported (today: missing) |

`home` + `vertex` is excluded by decision, not by structure: Vertex
credentials are work-issued and the home machine is not enrolled. Encode it
as an explicit rejection with a message, not as a silently missing file.

**If that decision reverses**, the change is deleting the rejection. The
`vertex-ai-full` segment is site-neutral (`**.googleapis.com`), the
site config already supplies home's telemetry endpoints, and gcloud ADC
uploads follow `access` regardless of site. The cell is empty by policy,
not unimplemented.

## 3. Rules

1. **One policy per sandbox, composed not hand-written.** OpenShell accepts
   a single policy file. That file is *generated* from `base` plus selected
   segments (§4), never edited directly.
2. **The generated policy is a per-sandbox artifact**, not a repo file. It
   lives at `~/sandboxes/<name>/openshell-policy.yaml`, peer to `manifest.json` (§5).
3. **No new `== "<profile>"` literals.** Dispatch reads `SITE`, `ACCESS`,
   and the selected segment list. Where behaviour is genuinely per-value,
   switch on the axis that owns it — never on a combined profile name.
4. **Every axis value has exactly one home for its data.** Site endpoints
   live in the site config; access credential lists live in the env-var
   group arrays in `sandbox.sh`; per-segment credentials live in the segment
   (§4.1). No value is defined twice.
5. **Values that differ per machine are never committed.** Tailnet names
   follow `~/source/standards/common/local-config-split.md`: committed
   `.example`, gitignored working copy. This repo is public.
6. **Private repos are acknowledged once per sandbox** — see §3.1.

### 3.1 Private repos

Two separate questions, currently answered by one blunt check.

**Which repos need no acknowledgement at all.** Today: no `--profile` (i.e.
work + Vertex) allows everything with no prompt; `personal` prompts for any
private repo. Under this model:

| site + access | prompt-free |
|---|---|
| `work` + `vertex` | all repos |
| `work` + `subscription` | owner `jewzaam` |
| `home` + `subscription` | owner `jewzaam` |

With the current matrix this collapses to a function of `access` alone —
`vertex` allows all, `subscription` allows the operator's own namespace.
Site contributes nothing today. Implement it keyed on `access`; revisit only
if `home` + `vertex` is ever enabled, which is the sole cell that could make
site matter.

**Acknowledgement is remembered, not re-asked.** Once a private repo has
been allowed into a sandbox, uploads and downloads of that repo proceed
silently. `manifest.json` already tracks repos per sandbox and is the
natural place to record the acknowledgement alongside the repo entry.
Removing the repo drops the record; adding it back asks again.

**Known defects to fix with this:**

- The prompt fires **twice on initial add** — once in `clone_repo`
  (`sandbox.sh:279`) and once in `upload_repo` (`sandbox.sh:314`). It should
  fire once, at the point the repo enters the sandbox.
- `--upload` of an already-acknowledged private repo does not prompt, which
  is the desired end state but appears to happen for the wrong reason:
  `upload_repo` gates on a locally-resolved `effective_profile`
  (`sandbox.sh:305-308`), while `guard_private_repo` re-reads the *global*
  `SANDBOX_PROFILE` (`lib.sh:16`) and returns immediately when it is empty.
  **Unverified** — worth confirming before relying on it, because the same
  gap would silence the prompt on paths where it is wanted.
- Download was never guarded at all. Under "acknowledge once" that is
  correct, but it is currently correct by omission rather than by design.

## 4. Policy composition

### 4.1 Segments

`policies/segments/<slug>.yaml`. Each file is a partial policy plus a `meta`
block that the builder strips before writing the applied policy.

```yaml
# policies/segments/jira-full.yaml
meta:
  description: Jira REST API — issues, search, attachments
  sites: [work]
  access: all
  default: none
  env:
    - JIRA_URL
    - JIRA_EMAIL
    - JIRA_USERNAME
    - JIRA_TOKEN
    - JIRA_API_TOKEN
    - JIRA_CLOUD_ID
  files: []
network_policies:
  jira_api:
    name: jira-full
    endpoints: [...]
    binaries:
      - { path: "/**" }
```

| `meta` field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `description` | shown in the picker; the slug alone should not have to explain itself |
| `sites` | list, or `all`. Slug is hidden when the current site is not listed |
| `access` | list, or `all`. Same filtering |
| `default` | `all`, `none`, or a list of `access` values for which the slug is pre-checked. Always unselectable by the operator |
| `env` | literal env var names written to `/sandbox/.env` when selected |
| `files` | host paths uploaded when selected |

`env` is a literal list, not a named group. The groups in `sandbox.sh:41-91`
are an implementation detail of one script; a config file that says
`JIRA_VARS` forces the reader to go find out what that contains. Spelling
the names out is the whole point of putting them in config.

**Where `env` values come from.** Three sources, and only three:

| Source | Which vars | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| host environment, verbatim | everything in a segment's `env` list | `sandbox.sh:1068-1073` copies `${!var}` for each name that is set |
| site config | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | §9.1 — the two values that cannot survive the move into a sandbox |
| computed by `sandbox.sh` | `PROJECT`, `SANDBOX_SOURCE_NAME`, `CLAUDE_DASHBOARD_HOST` | derived from the sandbox itself |

Three transformations exist today and stay in code rather than config,
because each is a one-off: the Jira alias fill-in
(`JIRA_USERNAME`↔`JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_TOKEN`↔`JIRA_API_TOKEN`,
`sandbox.sh:1077-1088`), the `SANDBOX_JIRA_*` scoped-token override
(`sandbox.sh:1091-1104`), and the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` path
rewrite (`sandbox.sh:1107-1109`). Each is documented where it happens.

**What `files` actually covers.** Two host directories are uploaded
conditionally today, and both are segment-scoped under this model:

| Host path | Sandbox path | Today's gate |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.config/gws-sandbox` | `/sandbox/.config/gws` | `profile != personal`, create + refresh (`sandbox.sh:594-606`) |
| `~/.config/gcloud` | `/sandbox/.config/gcloud` | `profile != personal`, create only (`sandbox.sh:1242-1245`) |

Everything else uploaded is unconditional and belongs to no segment:
`~/.claude/` minus excludes, `.bashrc`, `.env`, `.gitconfig` and the SSH
signing key, `bin/`, the system prompt, and the manifest
(`sandbox.sh:496-628`). The OAuth pair — `~/.claude.json` and
`~/.claude/.credentials.json` — is separate again: it is downloaded before a
`--recreate` and restored after (`download_claude_state`,
`upload_claude_state`), never uploaded on a normal create.

`~/.config/gcloud` belongs to `access: vertex`, not to a segment — it is
what Vertex authentication itself requires. `~/.config/gws-sandbox` belongs
to the `gws-full` segment.

**`base` is always included and is not a segment.** `policies/base.yaml`
holds exactly the fields identical across today's three policies: `version`,
`filesystem_policy`, `landlock`, `process`. Not shown in the picker, not
optional. Revisit only if a real case appears for varying it.

### 4.2 Slug naming

`<service>[-<site>]-<level>`, where `<level>` is the OpenShell `access:`
value the segment's endpoints actually carry:

| Slug suffix | OpenShell `access:` |
|---|---|
| `readonly` | `read-only` |
| `readwrite` | `read-write` |
| `full` | `full` |

`build-policy.py` validates that every endpoint in a segment carries the
level its slug claims, so the name cannot drift from the file. No
abbreviations — `jira-rw` was both abbreviated and wrong, since
`code.yaml:49-68` grants `full`.

The suffix names the **policy** level, not the credential scope. Where the
real limit comes from credentials rather than policy, the description says
so — see `gws-full`.

### 4.3 Inventory

| Slug | Source today | `sites` | `access` | `default` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vertex-ai-full` | `code.yaml:33-47` | all | `vertex` | all |
| `anthropic-full` | `personal.yaml:34-63` + `research.yaml:54-78` | all | all | `[subscription]` |
| `npm-readonly` | `code.yaml:70-79` | all | all | all |
| `pypi-readonly` | `code.yaml:130-144` | all | all | all |
| `debian-readonly` | `code.yaml:114-128` | all | all | all |
| `otel-local-full` | `code.yaml:81-90` | `work` | all | all |
| `otel-local-readonly` | `code.yaml:92-112` | `work` | all | none |
| `otel-tailnet-full` | none — new, gitignored | `home` | all | all |
| `otel-tailnet-readonly` | none — new, gitignored | `home` | all | none |
| `jira-full` | `code.yaml:49-68` | `work` | all | none |
| `gws-full` | none — new | `work` | all | none |

Filtering does the work the old profile names were doing: the tailnet slugs
never appear at work, `jira-full` and `gws-full` never appear at home, and
`vertex-ai-full` disappears under subscription.

**Telemetry slugs collapse to two per site.** `-full` is the push path (the
collector); `-readonly` is the query path (Prometheus and Loki). Prometheus
and Loki are not split: either a session can inspect its own telemetry or it
cannot, and no case exists for one without the other. They also cannot be
mixed across sites — a `work` sandbox querying the home cluster is not a
thing — which the shared `<site>` element in the slug makes visible.

The collector is `full` rather than `readwrite` because OpenShell has no
push-only level and the endpoints carry `access: full` today. It is
write-only in practice; the description should say so rather than the slug
implying reads happen.

Selecting `-readonly` without `-full` is allowed and coherent: querying
history without emitting anything. No dependency is enforced.

**`claude-platform` is deleted, not renamed.** Its endpoints
(`research.yaml:54-78`: `claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`,
`api.anthropic.com`, `statsig.anthropic.com`) are a strict subset of
`anthropic-api`'s (`personal.yaml:34-63`, the same five minus
`console.anthropic.com`). Two slugs for one host set is why the name meant
nothing. The merged `anthropic-full` is offered under **both** access
values, pre-checked only for `subscription` — which is exactly what the
research profile was reaching for: a Vertex sandbox that can also talk to
the Claude web properties.

`research.yaml` therefore does not survive at all. Its own header says open
web egress is blocked pending upstream issue #3, so nothing in it was "the
internet" — it was this host set plus duplicated boilerplate.

The missing `npm` and `debian` in `research.yaml` were drift, not intent.
Under per-slug selection with sane defaults the question cannot recur
silently.

**`gws-full` does not segment the Workspace APIs.** Its endpoint is the same
`**.googleapis.com` wildcard `vertex-ai-full` uses; what actually limits it
is the readonly OAuth scopes on the credentials the operator provisions on
the host (`sandbox.sh:13`). Two consequences to accept knowingly:

- The slug says `full` because the policy grants `full`. The readonly-ness
  lives in the credential, and the description must say that outright or the
  name misleads.
- Selecting it opens all of `googleapis.com`, including the Vertex inference
  endpoints, to a sandbox that may be running on `access: subscription`.
  Scoping the endpoints is the only fix, and it was judged not worth the
  maintenance.

`vertex-ai-full` and `gws-full` both allow `**.googleapis.com` but under
different `network_policies` keys, so selecting both is a redundant grant,
not a merge collision (§4.4).

The tailnet slugs contain a tailnet hostname, so their working copies are
gitignored with committed `.example` files beside them (rule 5). The local
slugs hold RFC1918 podman addresses and are committed as-is.

### 4.4 Merge

It is a recursive dict merge with list concatenation, and that is enough:

```python
def merge(a, b):
    for k, v in b.items():
        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(a.get(k), dict):
            merge(a[k], v)
        elif isinstance(v, list) and isinstance(a.get(k), list):
            a[k] += [x for x in v if x not in a[k]]
        else:
            a[k] = v
    return a
```

The one guard worth adding is an error on duplicate `network_policies` keys.
Without it, two segments defining the same key silently deep-merge into a
policy nobody wrote — endpoint lists concatenated across unrelated
intentions. Everything else can be left generic.

Lists concatenate rather than replace. That matters for
`filesystem_policy.read_only` and `.read_write`: a segment that adds one
path must not silently drop base's other seven.

Output keys are sorted so the same selection always produces a
byte-identical file and a change produces a real diff.

Implementation: `scripts/build-policy.py`, python3 + PyYAML, well under 50
lines. python3 is already a hard dependency (`sandbox.sh:520`).
*Unverified:* whether PyYAML is on the host. `uv run --with pyyaml` avoids a
system package and `uv` is already in the image (`Containerfile:23`).

### 4.5 `read-only` needs validating before it is trusted

`build-policy.py` can only check that a slug's suffix matches the `access:`
values in its own file (§4.2). It cannot check that OpenShell honours them.
Gotcha 2 records that *invalid* `access` values silently deny, but nothing
records what `read-only` *enforces* on an HTTP endpoint — whether it blocks
`POST`/`PUT` or is advisory. Until tested, every `readonly` suffix asserts
something unproven.

Test: from a sandbox with `pypi-readonly`, attempt an upload-shaped request
to `pypi.org` and record the result in `docs/troubleshooting.md`. If
`read-only` turns out to be advisory, rename the slugs or drop the
qualifier.

## 5. The applied policy is visible to the sandbox

### 5.1 Artifact

`build-policy.py` writes `~/sandboxes/<name>/openshell-policy.yaml`. That file is:

- what `openshell sandbox create --policy` and `openshell policy set`
  receive;
- uploaded to `/sandbox/source/openshell-policy.yaml`, peer to `manifest.json`;
- regenerated and re-uploaded whenever the segment selection changes (§6.3).

Embedding it in `manifest.json` was considered and rejected: OpenShell needs
a YAML file on disk regardless, so embedding means serialising YAML into
JSON and extracting it again on every use.

Upload goes through the existing staged-directory path that already carries
`manifest.json` (`sandbox.sh:612-627`) — gotcha 12 makes single-file upload
to a directory destructive.

### 5.2 Upload only. Never downloaded.

`openshell-policy.yaml` and `manifest.json` travel host → sandbox and never the other
way. The host copy is authoritative; the sandbox copy is a read-only mirror.
A session that edits either changes nothing, and no edit can propagate back
to the host, so a sandbox cannot widen its own policy or rewrite its own
repo list by editing a file.

This is a **requirement on `--download`**, not an accident of the current
code: the download path must pull only the repo directories listed in the
manifest, never the whole of `/sandbox/source/`. Add a test.

### 5.3 Why the sandbox gets a copy

A session that cannot see its own network policy discovers the boundary by
hitting it: a blocked host returns a 403 from the L7 proxy, the agent
retries, tries a mirror, tries different flags, and burns turns on something
no retry can fix. A readable policy turns that into one lookup.

### 5.4 System prompt contract

`config/sandbox-claude.md` gains a section stating:

- `/sandbox/source/openshell-policy.yaml` is the effective network and filesystem
  policy for this sandbox.
- It is **informational and read-only in effect**. Editing it changes
  nothing — enforcement lives outside the sandbox, and the file is never
  copied back to the host.
- Check it before concluding a host is unreachable and before proposing
  workarounds for a blocked request. A 403 from the proxy means "not in
  policy", not "transient".
- The policy **can change while the session is running**. When the operator
  says the policy, network policy, or segments have changed, **re-read the
  file** — do not rely on an earlier read. Changes are both additions and
  removals; a host that worked earlier may now be denied.

## 6. Selection and change

### 6.1 Inputs

| Axis | Flag | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| site | `--site` | only when `config/site.env` is absent; the answer is written there and not asked again |
| access | `--access` | single-select list |
| segments | `--segment` (repeatable) | multi-select, filtered by site + access, `default: true` pre-checked |

Site is deliberately **not** a per-sandbox prompt. It is a property of the
machine; asking every time invites a wrong answer that silently sends
telemetry to the wrong place.

Non-interactive runs (no TTY) with a missing required axis **fail**. They do
not fall back to a default.

### 6.2 Site config

Committed template `config/site.env.example`, gitignored working copy
`config/site.env`:

```sh
# config/site.env.example — copy to config/site.env and edit.
# The working copy is gitignored. Do not put real endpoints in this file.
SITE=work
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://172.30.0.10:4318
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
```

Only the values a sandbox needs live here. Bare-host telemetry settings are
the host's business, not this repo's (§9).

### 6.3 Prompt mechanics

Multi-select uses `fzf --multi`. The usual complaint is invisible selection
state — fzf marks chosen rows with a bare `>`. Fixable without changing
tool:

```sh
fzf --multi \
    --marker='[x] ' --pointer='  ' \
    --header 'TAB toggles, ENTER confirms' \
    --reverse
```

Defaults are pre-selected with a `start:` bind. *Unverified:* whether the
installed fzf accepts a multi-character `--marker` and the `pos()` action.

**Prompts must complete before VS Code launches.** `scode` resolves site,
access, and segments up front and only then spawns the editor. A prompt that
appears inside the VS Code terminal is missed — the operator is not watching
that pane, and the sandbox does not appear in the dashboard until its
session emits telemetry, so a stalled prompt is invisible from both
directions.

### 6.4 What can change on a running sandbox

| Axis | Change mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|
| segments | regenerate `openshell-policy.yaml`, `openshell policy set`, re-upload, tell the session to re-read | policy hot-swap already works (gotcha 14); `sandbox.sh --policy` already handles the async validation (gotcha 17) |
| access | `--recreate` | credentials, env vars, uploaded directories, and system-prompt stripping all differ; this is today's behaviour for switching to `personal` |
| site | not supported | it is the machine |

Segment change is the case that has no path today, and the reason
`--recreate` gets used for things that are not recreations.

## 7. Home telemetry over Tailscale — verified

Both concerns recorded here earlier were wrong. Measured from inside a
`home` + `subscription` sandbox with the rendered policy applied:

```
otel-collector.<tailnet>.ts.net:4318/v1/logs    405   receiver alive, rejects GET
prometheus.<tailnet>.ts.net:9090/-/healthy      403   policy denial
```

1. **The cluster exposes OTLP over HTTP, not only gRPC.**
   `setup-k3s/gitops/apps/otel-collector/values.yaml` enables the `otlp-http`
   port (4318) on the tailnet-exposed Service alongside 4317, and the
   Tailscale operator preserves the port. `405 Method Not Allowed` on a GET
   is the correct answer from a live OTLP receiver, so gotcha 13 is satisfied
   without any cluster-side change.
2. **MagicDNS resolves from inside a sandbox.** Resolution happens host-side
   at the L7 proxy and the host is on the tailnet, so an exact
   `<name>.<tailnet>.ts.net` host in the policy works. No Tailscale `100.x`
   fallback is needed, and the wildcard-validator question (gotchas 15, 16)
   never arises because `site.env` supplies exact hostnames.

The `403` on Prometheus confirms the push-only asymmetry holds at this site:
the collector is permitted, the query endpoints are not.

## 8. Open decisions

1. **`base` variability.** Fixed and always-on for the first round. If a
   segment ever needs to add a filesystem path, §4.4's list concatenation
   already supports it — no schema change needed.
2. **Does `read-only` enforce anything?** (§4.5) Blocks whether the
   `readonly` suffix is honest.
3. **fzf `--marker` and `pos()` support** on the installed version (§6.3).

## 9. Environment variables

### 9.1 `bin/claude.env` goes away

The sandbox stops carrying its own telemetry config file. Host environment
variables are carried forward into `/sandbox/.env` — which `sandbox.sh`
already does for `OTEL_VARS` (`sandbox.sh:70-83`, `:1059`) — and only the
values that cannot survive the move are overridden:

| Variable | Why it is overridden |
|---|---|
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | host reaches the collector on a host-local address; the sandbox reaches it through the proxy |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | host may use gRPC; a sandbox must use `http/protobuf` (gotcha 13) |

Both come from `config/site.env` (§6.2). This works because telemetry
destination follows the site, and a sandbox's site is its host's site — the
sandbox never has a site of its own.

Everything else — exporters, intervals, batching, log-detail flags — carries
from the host verbatim, so the sandbox cannot drift from the machine that
created it. Deleting `bin/claude.env` also removes the layer that silently
overrode `/sandbox/.env`: `claude-wrapper.sh:4` sources it *after* `.bashrc`
has sourced `.env`.

`config/bashrc` stays as it is. It is baked into the image
(`Containerfile:33`), so it cannot hold site-varying values without a
per-site image; `/sandbox/.env` is the layer that knows the site, and
`config/bashrc:9-13` already sources it.

### 9.2 `project`

`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is assembled at launch. `project` is the only
part that differs by runtime:

- **Bare host** — the working directory. Correct as `$(pwd)`; it is how a
  session is attributed to a repo.
- **Sandbox** — the sandbox name, read from `manifest.json` `.name`. The
  working directory is meaningless because `connect_sandbox()`
  (`sandbox.sh:196-200`) `cd`s to `/sandbox` or `/sandbox/source/` before
  launch, so every sandbox session currently reports
  `project=/sandbox/source/`.

The sandbox reads its own name rather than being told it, which keeps the
value consistent with the manifest by construction. `jq` is in the image
(`Containerfile:11`).

```sh
project="$(jq -r '.name' /sandbox/source/manifest.json 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
```

**Compatibility check.** The Grafana dashboards and Loki recording rules
already special-case sandboxes: `location` and `project_clean` prefer
`sandbox_source` when set and only fall back to `project`. Those paths are
unaffected, and the path-stripping regexes applied to `project` are no-ops
on a non-path value. What the change fixes is the `$project` template
variable, which today collapses every sandbox session into one
`/sandbox/source/` entry.

## 10. Doc drift found and fixed

`CLAUDE.md` claimed the personal profile skips OTEL entirely and that the
collector had been removed from `personal.yaml`. The code did the opposite:
`policies/personal.yaml:65-74` allows the collector, `sandbox.sh:1059`
includes `OTEL_VARS` for personal, and `sandbox.sh:1119-1121` tags personal
sessions. The entry was rewritten to describe the push-only shape that
actually ships, and the `host.containers.internal` all-ports gap was split
into its own entry — it is a real constraint, but it never applied to
`172.30.0.10`, which is a podman network address rather than the gateway
host. Its live consumer is the dashboard hook relay
(`CLAUDE_DASHBOARD_HOST`, `sandbox.sh:1113`).
